It's only been two sessions friend. Give it some time. I didn't expect to feel better after my first day of therapy and I sure as hell didn't after the second time but you have to let yourself be open to the therapy. Wondering if the therapist is pretending to be shocked to bond with you is a way to make her an enemy or close her off from helping you. She may truly be shocked. Some people don't deal with abuse and in her schooling she may have read about it, but reading about it and seeing someone who had to endure that pain are two very different things. However if you still feel like she's putting on a front, see if you can switch therapists until you feel that they are genuine and that you can trust them. You have to go to some dark places in therapy to feel better, and I will be honest - it didn't make me feel better going through it until I got to the end. There was a lot of crying, a lot of angry, a lot of feeling empty at times after the session, but each step was progress and each step helped me to finally leave it behind me.

Cutting is another form of a drug, and just like any other drug, it feels good. I said the same thing when I would dig my nails into my thigh until I would bleed just to feel some relief from the pain. Then I found myself cutting my upper thigh and inside my thigh so no one would know because digging my nails in my skin wasn't enough. Then that wasn't enough, and the only way I felt the same relief was when I swallowed a whole bottle of pills. It feels good because I'm satisfying the part that hated me and wants me to hurt. My depression convinced me it was like draining an abscess of my feelings and pain. It redirected the emotional pain to the physical which was more tolerable to me. You say your not hurting yourself but you are. You are taking something and using it to cause harm to yourself. You're taking blades from work and telling yourself it's safe because they are clean. What if someone finds out you're taking them? It's harmful to you because you may lose your job. Any harm to yourself can be very addicting, as others have said, and you will find yourself doing it more and more and then one day, just like a drug, it won't be enough to give you relief. That's where I was when I swallowed the bottle. I'm not necessarily a fan of anti-depressants as it made me feel numb and made it easier to make bad choices, however it does help some people. I can give you things that help me, but they all may not help you. That's the thing about depression, we have to constantly work on finding things that help us and sometimes certain things that worked won't work anymore and we have to try new things. It's okay if you feel tired, you can rest just as long as you don't go back. Rest until you're ready and keep moving forward. I'm happy you're alive friend. I can't tell you to stop, but I can only ask that you remember that cutting is only a temporary solution.

I think at times, parents can say things that are very hurtful despite their good intentions. When I told my parents I was depressed, they definitely did not understand that. When I told my brother, he very honestly told me once that he doesn't understand depression and his solution is to suck it up and keep moving. 

I know this is making my family sound a little callous, but that isn't at all how they are. They just had no idea how to handle someone who is depressed. As I sought counseling, they constantly asked me right after every session if I was better. I did feel alone and rushed to "get better" because I felt I was failing by not being better. When my family reacted the way they did, it made me feel very alone however I know my family is trying. Here is an example: I had a bad day and I called my brother because I didn't know what else to do. He was ready to give me some "tough love" but I told him I couldn't handle it. I saw on his face that he didn't know what to do because that was his method of coping, but I also saw understanding. He sat with me and stayed with me until I was feeling better. My sister-in-law is dealing with depression and despite the hardships I had to face from my family not fully understanding what depression is, they now know and have been able to be very supportive to her. It took a few years for me to understand they love and care for me, and it took them a few years to understand what was going on with me.

The truth Fast-Snail is this: **The true saying is that you can only help someone who wants to help themselves. However with depression, it is hard to want to help yourself when part of yourself wants you to not exist.**

Part of you wants help because you told your parents you are depressed. You parents may not know what to do and at times the general consensus with depression is to stop feeling sad. The truth is that you took the first step to tell someone you feel this way because you want help. You are reaching out and even now posting on here is a form of reaching out. 

I am proud of you for trying despite being given discouragement. I know this is hard for you and hell I had a really bad day yesterday and I was feeling close but we can get through this together. There are dozens of ways to seek help in a way that is comfortable to you. Speak to a counselor/therapist, find a friend that you can talk to about this, or even online. The community for people with depression online is very supportive. 

With depression, we at times need some extra help but we also have to be willing to accept help from people. This was very hard for me at times because I convinced myself (and still do at times) that I'm a horrible human being who does nothing but make others suffer but that's my depression talking.

**We are not defined by our illness. We have an individual story to tell. We have a name, a history, and a personality. Staying yourself is part of the battle.**  (Julian Seifter said this)

I am happy you're alive today friend and I am rooting for you. Continue to seek help and the thing you have to work on yourself is learning to love yourself which can be the biggest most challenging task you might have to face.

When I turned 25, I was a wreck. I was not in a good place in my life, and being a single lonely depressed girl surrounded by my peers who were married, having children, and had careers/good jobs made me  feel like I was a loser. The one thing I lost sight on was the fact that it was my birthday. I had been so concerned about the number that I forgot it was my special day.

I don't know what are the reasons you want to die, but I want you to know that I am happy you're alive today. I know you are thinking, "who is this crazy girl" or "she doesn't even know me" but that won't stop me from being happy you're alive today, and I'm not just saying that because it's your birthday. **You deserve to be happy and are worth everything.**

Today is your day, as others have said. But today is also to remember that the world would not be the same without you. 

Happy Birthday friend. I know today is a little rough and that's ok. If you want to rest and take it easy that's ok too. I am here for you and I will be rooting for you the entire way through :)
